comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROOT CAUSE (investigated before implementing; the ticket's stated mechanism is NOT what happens).

1. The close path already runs the LLM verifier OUTSIDE the write lock, and has since the
   gate was introduced (85a77b9cc8, 2026-06-18). `transition_close.close_ticket` calls
   `close_precheck._completion_precheck` (which runs `llm.verify_completion`) BEFORE
   `txn.transition_core`, and `transition_core` is where `lock.acquire` is first taken.
   An optimistic re-check under the lock also already exists (`pre_status_check` /
   `plan_review_recheck`), and `transition_core` re-reduces under the lock and raises
   ConcurrencyMismatch (exit 10) on a status mismatch. So the requested restructure
   (verify -> acquire -> re-check -> append -> release) is the code as it stands.

2. Instrumented proof. Wrapping `_store.lock.acquire` / `LockHandle.release` around a full
   `transition_compute(... in_progress -> closed)` with a stubbed verifier shows exactly four
   short acquisitions, ALL after the verifier returns, each bracketing only a store mutation:
   completion sidecar append, `txn.transition_core`, the SIGNATURE append, and
   `_compact_on_close`. A `write_lock_is_busy()` probe called from inside the stubbed verifier
   returns False (no lock dir, no ownership stamp).

3. What the real long holder is: COMPACT-ON-CLOSE. Caught live on this host, tracker
   .tickets-tracker (745M, ~4000 ticket dirs), pid 85578
   `rebar transition ethnogenic-centaurian-rat in_progress closed --ref c392d736`:
     20:51:46  COMPLETION_VERDICT commit   <- verifier already finished, no lock held
     20:51:54  STATUS commit               <- the close itself
     20:51:56  SIGNATURE commit
     20:51:59  .ticket-write.lock.d created, stamp pid=85578
     20:54:37  COMPACT commit              <- lock released
   i.e. ~2m38s of continuous write-lock hold by `_compact_on_close`, entirely after the LLM.
   Its stand-aside guard (`write_lock_is_busy`, bug 7084 / R3) is ineffective for the closing
   process itself: the close released the lock microseconds earlier, so the probe almost always
   reports "free" and compaction proceeds to take it. Bug 7084 measured this holder at 48.1s;
   on today's store it is minutes, and it scales with store size.

Conclusion: the 15+ minute hold observed for pid 61327 was compact-on-close (and/or repeated
acquisitions), not the verifier. The lock was never held across an LLM call. Implementing the
operator-specified restructure would be a no-op; fixing the real holder is different work with
different semantics (whether/when compaction may take the store lock), so it is being raised as
a separate ticket rather than folded in here. Escalating for a decision on how to re-scope this
bug.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: P0 ESCALATION + REFRAME (operator): this is a REGRESSION, not a longstanding design gap. transition_close.py:391-392 documents the verifier runs OUTSIDE the write lock, yet pid 61327's swan close held .ticket-write.lock.d continuously 20:35:52 -> ~20:51 during LLM verification (single hold; ctime stable across checks). Operator hint: 'The close path or the git lock path.' First deliverable = the regression commit. Suspects (recent close/lock-path commits): 61b49deaa6 (atomic staging, tonight), 8f6b6c9356 (close-without-signature restructure), cc69cc1179 (lock retries), 61058f6085 (stale-lock bound), 64451ec0bb (save-time warn), 746c1ba2e9, e0b3fdfc8e.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
P0 FOLLOW-UP: not a regression. The 15-minute hold is COMPACT-ON-CLOSE, and the incident's own
commit timeline proves the lock was acquired AFTER the verifier finished, not during it.

## The incident, from the tracker's commit log
pid 61327 was closing `repressive-delectable-swan` = 271c-e88f-3220-4c9b. Tracker commits:

    20:35:43  COMPLETION_VERDICT 271c   <- LLM verification FINISHED (sidecar written)
    20:35:47  STATUS            271c    <- the close itself (txn.transition_core)
    20:35:49  SIGNATURE         271c    <- PASS attestation signed
    20:35:52  .ticket-write.lock.d created   <- the hold you observed begins
    ...13m53s...
    20:49:45  COMPACT           271c    <- compact-on-close commits; lock released

The lock dir was born 3 seconds AFTER the SIGNATURE commit and 9 seconds after the verifier's
COMPLETION_VERDICT. One continuous hold, one ctime — exactly as observed — but its span is
`_compact_on_close`, not the verify phase. The verify phase held nothing.

## The same shape on every other close that hour
    f6e9: STATUS 20:20:01  SIGNATURE 20:20:04  COMPACT 20:22:31  -> 2m27s locked
    594b: STATUS 20:32:27  SIGNATURE 20:32:29  COMPACT 20:34:56  -> 2m27s locked
    271c: STATUS 20:35:47  SIGNATURE 20:35:49  COMPACT 20:49:45  -> 13m56s locked  (the incident)
    8fc2: STATUS 20:51:54  SIGNATURE 20:51:56  COMPACT 20:54:37  -> 2m41s locked

8fc2 was captured LIVE while investigating: `ls` of the lock dir at 20:54:35 showed stamp
`pid=85578`, a `rebar transition ... in_progress closed --ref c392d736` that had been running
4m27s and had held the lock since 20:51:59 — i.e. the same post-verify compaction span.

## Instrumented confirmation on current main (70679d3c21)
Two probes, both on the real close path:
- Wrapping `_store.lock.acquire` / `LockHandle.release` around a full `transition_compute`
  close shows exactly four acquisitions, ALL after the verifier returns, each bracketing only a
  store mutation: completion sidecar append, `txn.transition_core`, SIGNATURE append,
  `_compact_on_close`.
- A faithful sleeping-stub repro (stubbing only the innermost
  `llm.workflow.gate_dispatch.produce_completion_verdict`, so the REAL `verify_completion`
  wrapper still runs — snapshot handle resolution, `materialize_tickets`, `gate_read_root`)
  with a background thread sampling the lock dir every 20ms for the whole close:
  112 samples, 0 with the lock present during the verify phase; four post-verify holds of
  25ms, 25ms, 0ms, 48ms.

None of the seven listed commits (64451ec0bb, 61b49deaa6, 8f6b6c9356, 61058f6085, cc69cc1179,
746c1ba2e9, e0b3fdfc8e) moved acquisition ahead of the verifier. The verifier has run outside
the lock since the gate was introduced in 85a77b9cc8 (2026-06-18); `git log -S` over
transition.py / transition_close.py / close_precheck.py finds no commit that ever placed it
inside. There is no regression to revert.

## Why the stand-aside guard does not help
`_compact_on_close` probes `write_lock_is_busy` and skips when busy (bug 7084 / R3). That guard
cannot fire for the CLOSING process: the close released the lock microseconds earlier
(SIGNATURE at 20:35:49, probe at ~20:35:52), so the store reads free and compaction takes it.
7084 measured this holder at 48.1s; on today's 745M / ~4000-ticket store it is 2.5-14 minutes,
and it scales with store size. The lock-retry work (REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES, cc69cc1179) raises the
waiter's budget but cannot shorten a 14-minute holder.

## Scope
Fixing this changes WHEN compaction runs (skip / defer out-of-band / bound the lock-held
portion) — a user-visible change to close semantics beyond "move verification outside the
lock", which is already true. Raised separately as `choosy-arthrodic-barbet`
(cfcb-a023-09a0-42ad, linked discovered_from). Requesting a scope decision: re-point THIS
ticket at the compaction holder, or close it as not-a-bug (premise falsified) and run the fix
on choosy-arthrodic-barbet.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
NARROWING (P0): the 15 minutes is compact-on-close, and swan DID emit its COMPACT.

## Correction to the forensics
Swan's compaction did not "produce nothing to commit". Commit `72ff0358f7`,
`ticket: COMPACT 271c-e88f-3220-4c9b`, landed at **20:49:45** — 59 files changed (58 event
files renamed to `.retired` + 1 SNAPSHOT). So the span is bounded on both ends:

    20:35:49  SIGNATURE 271c            <- close write complete, store lock released
    20:35:52  .ticket-write.lock.d created (pid 61327)  <- _compact_on_close re-acquires
    20:49:45  COMPACT 271c committed    <- compaction done, lock released

**13m53s, one continuous hold, owned entirely by `_compact_on_close`.** Of the three suspects,
(a) compaction is the owner; (b) the best-effort push is NOT under the lock
(`push_after_commit` docstring: "Call AFTER the locked commit has released the store lock —
the push runs its own fetch/merge and must not nest inside the write lock", and it takes no
lock itself); (c) the atomic-staging change 61b49deaa6 touches `event_append`'s
`stage_and_commit`/`batch_stage_and_commit`, which `_compact_locked` does not use — it does its
own rename + `_git(add/commit)`.

## Why compaction can hold the store lock for a quarter of an hour
Raw git churn is NOT the cost. Measured on this tracker (54,931 tracked files, 745M):
`git status --porcelain` 0.185s, `git write-tree` 0.014s. The cost is a **nested lock plus a
large retry budget, taken while the store write lock is held**:

`_compact_locked` acquires `lock.acquire(tracker, timeout=30, attempts=2)` and then runs every
git op through `compact_txn._git` -> `gitutil.run_git_write` -> `_with_index_lock_retry`, which
opens with `_store_git_op_lock(tracker)` — a SECOND per-store advisory flock
(`.git/rebar-git-op.lock`). Budgets, all inside the held store lock:
  - `_STORE_GIT_LOCK_WAIT_S` = 30s waiting on the git-op lock (then degrades and proceeds);
  - `_INDEX_LOCK_ATTEMPTS` = 10 attempts, jittered backoff capped at `_INDEX_LOCK_BACKOFF_CAP_S` 5s;
  - each attempt is `_with_transient_head_retry` = up to `_TRANSIENT_HEAD_ATTEMPTS` 3 git children;
  - each child bounded by `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` = 120s.
Worst case for ONE `git add`/`git commit` is therefore tens of minutes, and the store write
lock has no ceiling of its own — `_compact_locked`'s 30s/2-attempt budget bounds only
*acquiring* it, never *holding* it. Six agents were writing this store concurrently during the
window, which is exactly the contention regime that walks that budget.

This is a hold-and-wait the lock module's own reasoning does not cover: `_store/lock.py`'s
docstring argues "neither leg waits on the other across processes there is no hold-and-wait
cycle => deadlock-free", but that argument is about the fcntl and mkdir legs of the SAME lock.
It says nothing about a second advisory lock acquired *inside* the store lock, which is what
every lock-held git op in compaction does.

Also note the c2ba bound the coordinator asked about: compaction does NOT escape it —
`run_git_write` applies the 120s watchdog — but 120s is a per-child bound multiplied by
3 x 10 retries, so the bound does not constrain the aggregate hold.

## Why the 7084 stand-aside does not save the close
`_compact_on_close` probes `write_lock_is_busy` and skips when busy. For the closing process
that probe is structurally useless: the close released the store lock ~3s earlier (SIGNATURE
20:35:49, probe ~20:35:52), so the store reads free and compaction takes the lock every time.

## Fix shape (NOT yet implemented — needs a scope decision)
The lock must bracket only the final ref mutation: do the fold (parse, reduce, build SNAPSHOT)
outside the store lock, then take the lock, re-check that no new events landed for the ticket
(optimistic re-check, same TOCTOU discipline the ACs ask for — a change since the fold means
discard this pass, not a stale write), rename + commit, release. Nested-lock waits and
multi-minute retry budgets must not sit inside the held store lock.

This changes WHEN compaction does its work relative to the close, which is a user-visible
close-semantics change beyond "move verification outside the lock" (already true), so I am
holding for a scope decision rather than implementing unilaterally. The ticket is also
unclaimed — no plan-review attestation — so implementing now would break claim-before-work.
Ready to proceed on either this ticket (re-pointed at the compaction holder) or
`choosy-arthrodic-barbet` (cfcb-a023-09a0-42ad), whichever you prefer.

RESOLUTION: closing as premise-falsified. The defect this ticket describes does not exist; the
real defect it was reaching for is now carried by `choosy-arthrodic-barbet`
(cfcb-a023-09a0-42ad, linked `supersedes` -> this ticket), which has the correct premise and
an operator-approved fix shape.

The ticket asserted that the close path acquires the tickets write lock and holds it across
the LLM completion verifier, and asked for a restructure to verify -> acquire -> re-check ->
append -> release. That restructure is already the code, and has been since the gate was
introduced in 85a77b9cc8 (2026-06-18). Three independent proofs, all recorded in the comments
above:

1. Code trace — `transition_close.close_ticket` runs `close_precheck._completion_precheck`
   (which calls `llm.verify_completion`) BEFORE `txn.transition_core`, which is where
   `lock.acquire` is first taken. The optimistic re-check the ACs ask for also already exists
   (`pre_status_check` / `plan_review_recheck`, plus `transition_core`'s under-lock re-reduce
   raising ConcurrencyMismatch/exit 10 on a status mismatch).
2. Instrumentation — wrapping `_store.lock.acquire` / `LockHandle.release` around a full close
   shows exactly four acquisitions, ALL after the verifier returns, each bracketing only a
   store mutation.
3. Faithful repro — stubbing only the innermost
   `llm.workflow.gate_dispatch.produce_completion_verdict` to sleep (so the REAL
   `verify_completion` wrapper still runs: snapshot handle resolution, `materialize_tickets`,
   `gate_read_root`), with a 20ms sampler over the whole close: 112 samples, 0 with the lock
   held during the verify phase; four post-verify holds of 25ms, 25ms, 0ms, 48ms.

And the incident's own commit timeline confirms it: for `repressive-delectable-swan`
(271c-e88f-3220-4c9b, pid 61327) the lock dir was created at 20:35:52 — 3 seconds AFTER the
SIGNATURE commit and 9 seconds after the verifier's COMPLETION_VERDICT — and released when
`ticket: COMPACT 271c` (72ff0358f7, 59 files) landed at 20:49:45. The 13m53s hold belongs to
`_compact_on_close`, not to any LLM call.

No code was written against this ticket and no acceptance criterion here is satisfiable as
stated, so the unchecked AC boxes stay unchecked deliberately: the falsification IS the
resolution record. Work continues on `choosy-arthrodic-barbet`.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem
The close path (`rebar transition <id> in_progress closed`) acquires the ONE tickets write lock (.ticket-write.lock + .ticket-write.lock.d) and holds it across the LLM completion verifier — a multi-minute agentic operation (observed 15+ min).

## Evidence (2026-08-12, this host)
- pid 61327 `rebar transition repressive-delectable-swan in_progress closed` held /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock.d from 20:35:52 for 15+ minutes (holder alive and healthy the whole time; stamp: rebar-lock v2 host=name-Joes-MacBook-Pro.local pid=61327).
- A concurrent session reported it could not close a ticket due to 'long-lasting locks on the tickets branch' during exactly this window.
- Earlier this session: an implementer lost 3 plan-review runs to flock contention from sibling agents; the lock-retry work (REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES, change cc69cc1179) treats the symptom (acquire timeouts) not the cause (verifier-length holds).

## Root-cause direction (operator-specified)
The close operation should NOT hold the write lock during the LLM completion verifier. Restructure to: run the verification BEFORE acquiring the write lock, then acquire, re-check the cheap invariants (status unchanged, attestation/current-material still valid — optimistic concurrency already exists on status), append the transition event, release. The lock should bracket only the store mutation, not the LLM phase.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The write lock is not held during any LLM call on the close path (verify with a test that asserts lock-dir absence while the verifier stub runs, or equivalent instrumentation).
- [ ] Optimistic re-check under the lock prevents TOCTOU: a status/material change between verify and append fails the close with exit 10 (ConcurrencyError semantics), not a silent stale write.
- [ ] Existing close-gate semantics unchanged: signature recording, --ref retargeting, force_close_reason, and the completion precheck behave identically.
- [ ] Concurrent-close regression test: two closes on different tickets do not serialize on the LLM phase.
compiled_state.title: transition close holds the tickets write lock for the whole LLM completion verification
